info.title: Aeolus API
info.description:
The machine-facing plane of Aeolus, a collaborative LaTeX and Typst editor you host yourself.

**Scope is not the ACL.** A token carries its minting user's document permissions, and both gates apply: a write-scope token minted by someone with viewer access still cannot write that document. See `docs/API.md`.

bearer.description: A token minted in the UI at /tokens. Shown once at creation; only a sha256 hash is stored.

doc_id.description: The document the selection came from. Read access is required.

prefer_higher_quality.description: Ask for the slower, better model. Costs more of the same quota.

error_context.description: A compile-error tail, which switches the prompt from rewrite to fix.

ErrorResponse.description: The uniform error envelope used by every route on this plane.

RateLimitedResponse.description: Rate limit exceeded. Honour the `retry-after` header.

ReadOnlyTokenResponse.description: The credential is valid but read-scope, and the method is a write. 403 rather than 401 is deliberate: re-authenticating cannot fix it, so a client that retries 401s by fetching a new token would loop forever.

retryable.description: Present and true when a retry may succeed.

ServiceUnavailableResponse.description: The request could not be served right now. Branch on `error`.

id.description: The public half of the credential. Safe to log.

disabled_at.description: When set, every session AND every API token of theirs is refused.

archived_at.description: When set, the document is read-only: writes return 422 `archived`.

yjs_doc_id.description: The CRDT document backing a text file. Null for blobs and folders.

size_bytes.description: For text files this is computed from the CRDT, not stored.

kind.description: `user` for a named checkpoint, `auto_open` for one the editor took.

pdf_url.description: Relative to /api. Null unless the compile succeeded.

error.description: The engine log excerpt, on failure.

warnings.description: Non-fatal findings on a successful compile — e.g. a font the PDF references but does not embed, which renders blank on machines without it. Empty when clean. Do not ship a PDF that carries one without reading it.

is_published.description: An unpublished template is a draft and is invisible to non-admins.

yjs_doc_id.description: The backing document. Editable by an admin like any other.

rev.description: The revision the file is actually at now.

warnings.description: The warnings recorded on that compile — see Compile.warnings.

actor_email.description: Captured at event time, so it survives the account.

AssistStream.description: An SSE stream. See the description for the event grammar; the body is not JSON and this is a text/event-stream, not a string.

ticket.description: Opaque. Store it nowhere; it expires in minutes.

get.description: Returns the user the token acts as — the identity the document ACL is evaluated against — and the scope of the credential used. The cheapest way to check a token works, and to discover its scope without taking a 403.

patch.description: The only thing you can change about yourself — an administrator owns and is read-only. A token does this as the user who minted it.

get.description: Hourly and daily request counts and the daily token allowance, for the user this token acts as. Worth checking before a batch job: the quota is per user, so a token spends its owner's allowance.
Documents the token's user owns or collaborates on, newest-updated first. Admins see every non-template document. Template-backing documents never appear.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Defaults to `active`, which hides archived documents.

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Admin-only; ignored for everyone else. Soft-deleted documents.

post.description: **Admin only.** Everyone else creates documents by forking a curated template, which is the brand-controlled path. A non-admin token gets 403 `forbidden` here however wide its scope.

404.description: No such document — OR one this token's user cannot read. The two are deliberately indistinguishable, so the API never confirms a document exists to someone without access.

get.description: The whole tree — text files, uploaded blobs and folders — ordered by path. `size_bytes` for a text file is computed from its CRDT rather than stored, so it reflects unsaved-to-snapshot edits too.

post.summary: Create an empty text file or a folder
post.description: Paths are relative, `/`-separated, and reject traversal. A text file gets a fresh CRDT document; a folder gets neither that nor storage.

get.description: Returns the file as a plain string, materialised from its CRDT — the same source the compile worker reads, so what you get is what would compile. `rev` is the revision you read at: pass it back as `if_rev` on a write to make the write conditional.

put.description: Applies the new text as a single CRDT transaction against the live document, so a collaborator with the file open stays coherent instead of desynchronising — and is told to re-bootstrap. Supply `if_rev` for optimistic concurrency; omit it and the last writer wins.

if_rev.description: The `rev` from a prior read. Refuses with 412 if it moved.

patch.description: Renaming a folder rewrites every descendant's path in the same transaction. The main entrypoint (`main.tex` / `main.typ`) cannot be renamed — the compile worker finds it by path.

delete.summary: Delete a file or an empty folder
delete.description: A non-empty folder is refused with `folder_not_empty` and a count, rather than cascading deletions you did not ask for. The main entrypoint cannot be deleted. A blob's bytes are only removed when nothing else references them — forks share a template's objects.

post.description: multipart/form-data. `file` is the payload; `path` is where it lands (defaults to the uploaded filename). Allowlisted by extension (.png .jpg .jpeg .pdf .bib .cls .sty .ttf .otf .csv), 25 MB per file and 200 MB per project.

get.description: Published templates, newest-updated first. Admins also see drafts.

post.description: **Admin only.** Creates the template and its backing document, which an admin then edits like any other document to fill in the content.

404.description: No such template — or an unpublished one, to a non-admin. Deliberately indistinguishable, as with documents.

patch.description: **Admin only.** Publishing is `is_published: true` — that is what makes a template visible and forkable by everyone else.

404.description: No such template — or an unpublished one, to a non-admin. Deliberately indistinguishable, as with documents.

delete.description: **Admin only.** Soft delete. The backing document goes with it, or it would linger in admin listings as an orphan nobody can reach. Documents already forked from it are unaffected.

404.description: No such template — or an unpublished one, to a non-admin. Deliberately indistinguishable, as with documents.

post.summary: Fork a template into a new document
post.description: The way a non-admin creates anything. Copies **every** text file — not just the entrypoint — each with its own CRDT, so `\input` siblings survive. Blobs are copied by reference: a fork is a snapshot of the template at fork time, and the template later deleting a logo does not pull it out from under existing forks.

404.description: No such template — or an unpublished one, to a non-admin. Deliberately indistinguishable, as with documents.

post.description:
Enqueues a job and returns immediately with `202`. Poll `GET /docs/{id}/compile/{jobId}` until `status` leaves `queued`/`running`, then fetch the PDF from `/download`.

Rate limited to **6 per minute per token** — each one is a container-minute of Tectonic or Typst.

get.description:
**204 when the document has never compiled successfully** — a normal state, not an error (ADR 0018).

`is_current` tells you whether this PDF still matches the project, so you can skip a rebuild. It is not a revision comparison: editing a sibling file or adding an image does not move `rev`, so the server compares timestamps across the whole project and errs toward `false`.
Poll this after starting a compile. On failure, `error` carries the engine log excerpt — which is what you want in CI output.
Streams `application/pdf`. This is the only way to the bytes — there is no public or presigned URL. `?inline=1` flips Content-Disposition.

The source↔PDF position map from the most recent successful LaTeX compile. **204** when there is none — never compiled, a Typst document (Typst emits no synctex, permanently), or the blob has gone. None of those is an error the caller can act on differently.
Unlike `/synctex/latest`, an absent map here is a **404** — you named a specific job, so "it has none" is an answer about that job.

get.summary: Download the whole project as a zip
get.description:
Every file: text rendered from its CRDT to UTF-8, blobs verbatim. The way to get a project out of Aeolus.

Rate limited to **6 per minute per token** — it loads the whole project into memory.

Version history for **one file**, newest first. Aeolus keeps history per file, not per project, so `fileId` selects which — omitted, it is the project's first text file.

Slices belonging to a project checkpoint are excluded; they are not free-standing history. Listing also sweeps auto-open checkpoints older than 30 days.

post.summary: Take a checkpoint of one file
post.description: Snapshots the file's current content under a label. Take one before a scripted bulk edit and you have a way back.

get.summary: Download a checkpoint's raw CRDT snapshot
get.description: The encoded Yjs update, as `application/octet-stream`. Useful for an external archive; to get readable text, restore it and read the file's content instead.

post.summary: Restore one file to a checkpoint
post.description: Applies the snapshot as a CRDT transaction against the live document and tells any open editor to re-bootstrap — so this converges with a collaborator rather than fighting them. The restore is itself a new revision, so it can be undone by restoring a later checkpoint.

post.summary: Take a checkpoint of the whole project
post.description:
Snapshots **every** text file and pins the current blob set under one label — the thing to do before a scripted change that touches more than one file.

Rate limited to **6 per minute per token**.

post.summary: Restore the whole project to a checkpoint
post.description:
Restores every captured text file and replaces the blob set wholesale.

`blobs_missing` names any pinned object whose bytes have since gone — the restore still completes for everything else rather than failing outright, and tells you what did not come back.

delete.description: Removes the checkpoint and its file slices. The pinned S3 objects are not deleted here — the file-delete path is what frees bytes once nothing references them.

get.description: **Admin only.** Includes when each was last seen.

patch.description: **Admin only.** Grant or revoke admin, or correct a display name.

delete.description:
**Admin only**, and irreversible. Every document they own is transferred to *you* first, in the same transaction — `docs.owner_id` is RESTRICT precisely so a delete cannot silently take someone's drafts with it. Their tokens and sessions go by cascade.

Prefer `disable` unless you actually need the row gone.

422.description: You cannot delete or disable your own account.

post.description: **Admin only.** The reversible alternative to deleting, and it is immediate: a disabled user is refused on every request, which kills their sessions **and every API token they minted** without either having to be enumerated. This is the offboarding lever.

422.description: You cannot delete or disable your own account.

post.description: **Admin only.** Lifts the disable. Tokens they minted work again.

422.description: You cannot delete or disable your own account.

get.description:
**Admin only.** Newest first, cursor-paginated on `occurred_at` so a page boundary cannot skip or repeat a row the way an OFFSET can while new events land.

A trailing dot on `action` makes it a prefix: `doc.` matches every document action. **Events from `/api/v1` carry `metadata.via = "api_token"` and the token id**, so one query answers "what did automation do".

Retention is 30 days, enforced as a side effect of reading.

post.description:
Server-Sent Events. The response is `text/event-stream`; read it with an SSE client, not `response.json()`.

Four event types, each with a JSON `data` payload:

| `event:` | `data:` | |
|---|---|---|
| `chunk` | `{"text":"…"}` | A fragment of the suggestion. Concatenate in order. |
| `usage` | `{"usage":{"input_tokens":…,"output_tokens":…,"cache_creation_input_tokens":…,"cache_read_input_tokens":…}}` | Emitted once, near the end. |
| `done` | `{}` | The suggestion is complete. |
| `error` | `{"error":"…"}` | The model failed **after** the stream opened. |

Lines beginning `:` are keepalive comments, sent every 15s so an idle proxy does not drop a long generation; ignore them.

**A failure can arrive two ways.** Anything checkable before the first byte — the document ACL, your quota, the global spend cap, an unconfigured service — is an ordinary JSON status response. Once the stream is open the status is already 200, so a later failure can only be an `error` event. A client that treats 200 as success will report a failed generation as an empty one.

The quota is per user, not per token. Requires a write-scope token.

404.description: No such document, or none you can read (ADR 0003).

429.description: `rate_limited` is the plane's 120/min budget and carries `retry-after`. `quota_exceeded` is your Claude-assist allowance and carries no header at all — the answer is not "wait a moment". Read `GET /ai/quota`.

503.description: `ai_unavailable`: no API key configured. `quota_exceeded` at 503: the whole deployment hit its daily spend cap, not you.

post.summary: Mint a ticket for the collaboration WebSocket
post.description:
Returns a short-lived, document-bound ticket to pass as `?ticket=…` on the `wss://` upgrade URL. Valid for 5 minutes and multi-use within that window; re-mint around reconnects rather than holding one open.

**You only need this to speak Yjs.** To read or write a file, use `GET`/`PUT /docs/{id}/files/{fileId}/content` — those are the operations this API is shaped for. The socket is for live co-editing.

**What a ticket is not.** Once redeemed it is outside this plane: the socket has no scope gate and no rate limit, and the CRDT's own edits are not audited operation by operation. A write-scope token is required to mint one for exactly that reason — a read token must not be able to reach a channel that cannot enforce its scope. Every mint is audited.

404.description: No such document, or none you can read (ADR 0003).
